title: Queso de Bola guava: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Queso de Bola guava: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Queso de Bola guava is a guava variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Queso de Bola is a registered guava variety, also sold or known as bayabas Queso de Bola or NSIC Gv 01. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Gv 01. Jaime Goyena, Sr bred it.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for bayabas Queso de Bola or NSIC Gv 01, this is the same guava. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [guava variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
Key facts about Queso de Bola guava

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller
rows: bayabas Queso de Bola, NSIC Gv 01

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Queso de Bola was about 3 years old when it was registered. It bears regularly, with fruit in August September. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit guava fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Queso de Bola weighs about 575 g grams, and its shape is oblate. The flesh is white and crispy. Its sweetness measured 10.26 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 100 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as August September, bearing regular.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits August to September, bears early.
**Fruit:** Flattened round, about 575 g, yellow green, finely smooth skin, crisp, sweet, fiberless white flesh, pleasant aroma, about 10 Brix.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the only registered guava: big, round, crisp fruit of about 575 g. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Queso de Bola guava

Pick a variety by the fruit your buyers pay for: its size, sweetness and flesh, and how regularly the tree bears. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is bayabas Queso de Bola the same as Queso de Bola?
items.a: Yes. bayabas Queso de Bola is another name for Queso de Bola, registered as NSIC 2002 Gv 01. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Queso de Bola?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
